title: Over Half of Gen Z Plan to Job Hunt in 2026
paragraphs: For older generations, spending a whole career at one company was pretty common.
But, as Bob Dylan sang, "the times they are a-changin'." For many young workers today, moving from one employer to another is no longer something to avoid — it's part of building a career.

A new survey by US recruitment company Robert Half found that 55% of American workers in Generation Z — usually defined as those born in the late 1990s and early 2000s — plan to look for a new job before the end of 2026. That's a big increase from 32% a year earlier.
More than half said they believe changing employers could help them earn more.

And they may be right. In September, Bank of America found that people changing jobs were getting bigger pay increases than at any time in the past three years, with Gen Z workers seeing the biggest benefit.
But money isn't the only reason young workers are looking around.

Robert Half found that, among those planning to look for another job, 56% wanted better benefits, such as health insurance, flexible hours and help with travel costs. Half also said they couldn't really grow in their present job.

And AI is bringing new pressures to the workplace too. Although 87% of those surveyed said they use AI for work, nearly one in four said bringing AI into their daily work had led to burnout. Many felt pressure to be more productive, worried about losing their job if they didn't use new tools, or found it difficult to learn new things all the time.
And among those looking for new work, 37% said they were worried about keeping their AI skills up to date.
So for Gen Z, the times really are changing — and changing jobs may be one way to keep up.
